00385/head_neck.schedule: Six weekly cisplatin doses with radiotherapy. Radiotherapy follows cisplatin on cisplatin days. If radiotherapy is cancelled, cisplatin is postponed until RT resumes.
00385/head_neck.testing: FBC, renal and liver tests at baseline and before each weekly cycle; audiology/clearance when clinically indicated.
00385/head_neck.patient_action: Report hearing changes, numbness, fever, reduced intake and swallowing problems early. Do not imply fixed safe days between doses.

00385/nasopharyngeal.preserve_context: Keep the nasopharyngeal indication and radiation plan distinct.

00387.schedule: Three cisplatin doses every 21 days during radiotherapy, subject to response/tolerance; radiotherapy follows cisplatin on treatment days.
00387.testing: FBC, renal and liver profile each cycle; assess hearing and neuropathy history each cycle, with audiology/clearance when indicated.
00387.support: Dental and nutrition consultation before treatment. Prescribed hydration/antiemetics; encourage oral hydration for 24 hours according to the individual plan.

00207/head_neck.schedule: Cetuximab loading dose one week before radiotherapy, then weekly through RT. This is the locally advanced, platinum-ineligible context.
00207/head_neck.testing: Blood count, renal/liver profiles and electrolytes. Continue monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last cetuximab dose.
00207/head_neck.support: Antihistamine/corticosteroid premedication; skin/nail care and urgent infusion, breathing and eye warnings. Patients must not restart treatment themselves because a rash has improved.
00207/head_neck.observation_conflict: Retain the NCCP first-two-infusion versus EMA every-infusion observation difference for team confirmation; do not promise automatic shortening.

00207.preserve_context: CRC monotherapy retains RAS-wild-type/EGFR/prior-treatment criteria. Do not add radiotherapy from the head/neck context.
propagate: Electrolyte follow-up after the final dose

00705.schedule: Up to six 21-day combination cycles, then pembrolizumab alone every 21 days. Six cycles is not the entire treatment duration. FU can use daily 22-hour infusions or two 48-hour infusions as locally agreed; keep these as alternative calendars.
00705.testing: DPD status before first FU unless already tested. Blood count, kidney/liver profiles and glucose each cycle; thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks; baseline virology screening.
00705.new_caution: Renal impairment can affect uracil-based DPD results; the team may consider genetic testing. This does not negate known complete DPD deficiency.
00705.medicine_review: Tell the team about systemic steroids and other immunosuppressants. Medicines used after treatment for immune toxicity have a separate role.
00705.patient_action: Immune effects can occur after the last dose. Retain urgent-contact instructions throughout maintenance and after stopping.

00706.schedule: Up to six 21-day combination cycles with cisplatin day 1 and FU days 1–4, then pembrolizumab alone every 21 days. Preserve the cisplatin fluids and longer treatment day.
00706.testing: DPD before FU; blood count, renal/liver profiles and glucose each cycle; thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks. Audiology/clearance when clinically indicated.
00706.medicine_review: Retain the baseline-versus-immune-management distinction for systemic immunosuppressive medication.
00706.patient_action: Report hearing changes, numbness, poor intake, diarrhoea, mouth soreness and immune warning symptoms. A platinum switch is a Consultant decision, not patient self-management.

shared_notes: Preserve detailed anatomy and all unique offline handbook content.
Do not route recurrent/metastatic cetuximab maintenance from 00417/00418 into the 00207 head/neck radiotherapy portal. Retain the maintenance context within the new combination suites.
Do not introduce patient dose percentages from these clinician decision guards.
Do not invent fixed tumour-marker or imaging schedules; monitoring follows the individual Consultant plan.
